## What it will cover

::: {.mm-stub-outline}
- SMILES: reading, writing and canonicalising molecular structures
- RDKit: parsing, drawing and sanitising molecules
- Descriptors: molecular weight, logP, TPSA, H-bond counts, rotatable bonds
- Fingerprints: Morgan/ECFP bit vectors and what the bits mean
- Tanimoto similarity and nearest-neighbour search
- Lab 5: recompute the ESOL descriptors from SMILES and rebuild the Chapter 2 model
:::

## Planned learning outcomes

1. Convert SMILES to RDKit molecules, compute descriptors and fingerprints, and build an X matrix from them.
2. Explain what a Morgan fingerprint encodes and compute Tanimoto similarities.
3. Find the nearest neighbours of a query molecule in a library and judge whether they are chemically sensible.

## In the meantime

Everything here builds on Part I, in particular the evaluation habits of [Chapter 2](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/index.html). Episode [2.6](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/06-pipelines-leakage.html) already introduces the group splits that become scaffold splits here.
